title.value: Brainhack: Developing a culture of open, inclusive, community-driven neuroscience
title.justification: The title is directly taken from the paper's title section, indicating the focus on Brainhack events in neuroscience.
title.quote: Brainhack: Developing a culture of open, inclusive, community-driven neuroscience

analysis.description: The paper discusses Brainhack, an innovative meeting format that promotes scientific collaboration and community-driven problem-solving in neuroscience through decentralized gatherings. It highlights the benefits of such events in fostering open science, inclusivity, and interdisciplinary collaboration.

type.justification: The paper is mostly a theoretical exploration of the Brainhack concept, discussing its principles, methodologies, and its impact on the neuroscience community rather than empirical data or experimental results.
type.quote: In the following NeuroView, we aim to address two key questions about the merits of a Brainhack.

name.justification: The paper's focus is on neuroscience, discussing how Brainhack events contribute to this field.
name.quote: Brainhack events complement these formats in neuroscience with decentralized 2- to 5-day gatherings.

name.justification: The paper emphasizes open science practices, such as reproducible methods and data sharing, as central to Brainhack events.
name.quote: Brainhack events...foster a new research culture that celebrates open science, collaboration, and diversity, unlocking opportunities for scientific progress.

name.justification: BrainBox is mentioned as a significant project originating from Brainhack that enables real-time collaborative segmentation of MR images online.
name.quote: Its successor, BrainBox (https://brainbox.pasteur.fr/), has evolved to enable real-time collaborative segmentation of any MR image accessible online.

is_contributed.justification: BrainBox is described as having originated from Brainhack, indicating it as a contribution of these events to neuroscience.
is_contributed.quote: The project originated at the first Brainhack in 2012: The Brain Catalogue... Its successor, BrainBox...

is_executed.justification: The paper describes BrainBox conceptually as a tool for collaboration, without detailing execution specifics like CPU or GPU usage.
is_executed.quote: BrainBox has been used in many subsequent Brainhack projects, research collaborations, and science outreach events.

is_compared.justification: There is no mention of BrainBox being numerically compared to other models in the paper.
is_compared.quote: BrainBox has been used in many subsequent Brainhack projects, research collaborations, and science outreach events.

referenced_paper_title.justification: The reference paper detailing the origins and functions of BrainBox is cited in the document.
referenced_paper_title.quote: Heuer, K., Ghosh, S.S., Robinson Sterling, A., and Toro, R. (2016). Open Neuroimaging Laboratory. Research Ideas and Outcomes 2, e9113.

name.justification: Nighres is mentioned as a tool developed during Brainhack events for high-resolution neuroimaging data processing.
